| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| πικρὸς ὀϊστός (22.8) | "a bitter arrow" | "a bitter arrow" | "cruel arrow", "sharp arrow" (ὀξύς), "biting"; πικρός keeps the "bitter" of πικρόγαμοι |
| ἄμφωτος (of a cup, 22.10; ἀμφί + οὖς 'ear') | "two-eared" | "with two handles" | "two-handled" in `l` (hides the ear), "double" (reserved for ἀμφικύπελλον), "twin-eared" |
| αὐλὸς αἵματος (22.18; αὐλός 'pipe, tube') | "a spout of blood" | "a jet of blood" | "pipe" (the flute-word), "stream", "fountain", "gout" |
| ἁπαλὸς αὐχήν (22.16) | "the tender neck" | "his tender neck" | "soft neck", "delicate neck", "slender" |
| εἴδατα (plural of εἶδαρ, 22.20, 22.85; same half-line twice) | "the viands" | "the food" | "dishes", "meats" (κρέα), "victuals" in `i`; kept identical at both lines; σῖτος stays "food" |
| χολωτὸς ἔπος (22.26, χολωτοῖσιν ἐπέεσσι) | "angry words" | "angry words" | "bitter words" (πικρός), "wrathful", "furious" |
| πείρατα ὀλέθρου (22.33 ἐφῆπτο, 22.41 ἐφῆπται; same phrase twice) | "the limits of destruction" | "the limits of destruction" | "the ends of destruction", "the cords/nooses of destruction" (the rope image goes in the note only); follows the table's πείρατα "limits" |
| ἐεικοσάβοιος (22.57; ἐείκοσι + βοῦς) | "worth twenty oxen" | "worth twenty oxen" | "twenty-ox", "of twenty cattle", "twentyfold" |
| ἐν μοίρῃ (22.54, πέφαται) | "in due portion" | "as was due" | "fate" (reserved for μοῖρα alone), "justly", "in his lot" |
| ἀρεσσάμενοι κατὰ δῆμον (22.55) | "having made amends throughout the land" | "make amends through the land" | "having appeased" (reserved for the 8.396 row), "pacified", "having satisfied the people" |
| ἀκαχμένον ἀμφοτέρωθεν (of a sword, 22.80) | "on both sides pointed" | "sharpened on both sides" | "double-edged" (reserved for ἄμφηκες), "two-edged", "pointed at both ends" |
| εὖχος (22.7, πόρῃ εὖχος) | "a boast" | "the triumph" | "glory" (reserved for κῦδος), "renown" (κλέος), "vaunt" |
| ἴσκεν (22.31) | "supposed it so" | "imagined" | "said", "was saying" (the note gives both senses of ἴσκω) |
